content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Introduction to Generics** as part of **Generics and Type-System Design**. Generics preserve relationships between types and reduce unsafe casts; type constraints and variance should be as simple as the API requires. Use the subtopics—Generic Classes, Generic Functions, Type Parameters and Type Inference—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Generic Classes
items.text: Generic Classes should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Generic Functions
items.text: Generic Functions describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.
